doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Humility, spirituality and hating one's own records
summary: Cooper says a supreme being plays through him; both dislike hearing their records, unlike Dinah Washington.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: That speaks of a certain humility. And talk to us about that. About the spirituality and staying humble before the music.

Well okay, well actually I don’t play the trombone. Okay, a supreme being plays the trombone through me. I am the instrument. You understand what I’m saying? So I mean I just put that clearly now, you understand what I’m saying?
But he’s a good trombone player, though.

And like a lot of guys say well, they say well listen, I can just sit here because he never called me for a job or anything so I mean, I’ve got to get [inaudible] in the world. That’s the way I see it.
It’s easy to be humble playing jazz because it never comes out the way you want it to. You know, ‘cause that thing is always fighting back at you.
And I hate to hear myself on records.
I say I could of done this, why didn’t I do that? I could have done this. You understand what I’m saying? I say why? Why did I do that? Something else man.
I don’t think anybody likes to hear their own records.
In the dressing room, in the theater like the Potter Theater, like all between the shows she’s playing her records all day long.
Oh that’s what I’m talking about.
